annotations.title: Not to teach othervvise.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> The proper marke of Heretikes & false preachers, is, to teach othervvise or contrarie to that vvhich they found taught and beleeued generally in the vnitie of the Catholike Church before their time: al doctrine that is odde, singular, nevv, differing from that vvhich vvas first planted by the Apostles, and descended dovvne from them to al nations and ages folovving vvithout contradiction, being assuredly erroneous. <mn>[2]</mn> The Greeke vvord vvhich the Apostle here vseth, expresseth this point so effectually, that in one compound terme he giueth vs to vvit, that an Heretike is nothing els but an after-teacher, or teacher-othervvise: vvhich euen it self alone is the easiest rule euen for the simple to discerne a false Prophet or preacher by, specially vvhen an heresie first beginneth. <mn>[3]</mn> Luther found al Nations Christian at rest and peace in one vniforme faith, and al preachers of one voice and doctrine touching the B. Sacrament and other Articles: so that vvhat so euer he taught against that vvhich he found preached and beleeued, must needes be an other doctrine, a later doctrine, an after-teaching or teaching-othervvise, and therfore consequently must needes be false. And by this admonitiō of S. Paul, al Bishops are vvarned to take heede of such, and specially to prouide that no such odde teachers arise in their dioceses.

notes.text: Teaching othervvise then the doctrine receiued, is a special marke of Heretikes.

annotations.title: To fables.
annotations.text: He speaketh specially of the Ievves after-doctrines and humane constitutions repugnant to the lavves of God, vvhereof Christ giueth vvarning Mt. 23 and in other places, vvhich are conteined in their Cabala and Talmud: ◦ generally of al heretical doctrines, vvhich in deede, hovv so euer the simple people be beguiled by thē, are nothing but fabulous inuentions, as vve may see in the Valentinians, Manichees, and others of fable old: by the brethren of loue, Puritans, Anabaptistes, and Caluinistes of our time. For vvhich cause Theodorete entitleth his booke against Heretikes, Hereticarum fabularum, Of Heretical fables.

annotations.title: Questions.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Let our louing brethren consider vvhether these contentious and curious questionings and disputes in religion, vvhich these vnhappie heresies haue ingendered, haue brought forth any increase of good life, any deuotion, or edification of faith and religion in our daies. and then shal they easily iudge of the truth of these nevv opinions, and the end that vvil folovv of these innouations. In truth al the vvorld novv seeth they edifie to Atheisme and no othervvise.

annotations.title: The end Charitie.
annotations.text: Here againe it appeareth, that Charitie is the cheefe of al vertues, and the end, consummation, and perfection of al the lavv and precepts. and yet the Aduersaries are so fond as to preferre faith before it, yea to exclude it from our iustification. Such obstinacie there is in them that haue once in pride & stubbernes forsaken the euident truth. ◦ Charitie doubtles vvhich is here commended, is iustice it self, and the very formal cause of our iustification, as the vvorkes proceding thereof, be the vvorkes of iustice. Charitas inchoata ( saith S. Augustine ) inchoata iustitia: Charitas prouecta, prouecta iustitia: Charitas magna, magna iustitia: Charitas perfecta, perfecta iustitia est. Charitie novv beginning, is iustice beginning: Charitie grovven or increased, is iustice grovven or increased: great Charitie, is great iustice: perfect Charitie, is perfect iustice. Li. de nat. & grat. c. 70.

notes.text: Charitie the very formal cause of our iustification.

annotations.title: Desirous to be Doctors.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> It is the proper vice both of Iudaical and of Heretical false teachers, to professe knovvledge and great skill in the Lavv and Scriptures, being in deede in the light of the learned most ignorant of the vvord of God, not knovving the very principles of diuinitie, euen to the admiration truely of the learned that reade their bookes or heare them preach.

annotations.title: The lavv not made to the iust.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> By this place and the like, the Libertines of our daies vvould discharge them selues ( vvhom they count iust ) from the obedience of lavves. But the Apostles meaning is that the iust man doth vvel, not as compelled by lavv or for feare of punishment due to the transgressors thereof, but of grace & mere loue tovvard God & al goodnes, most vvillingly, though there vvere no lavv to commaund him.

annotations.title: Deliuered to Satan.
annotations.text: [1] Hymenæus and Alexander are here excommunicated for falling from their faith & teaching heresie: an example vnto Bishops to vse their spiritual povver vpon such. In the primitiue Church, corporal affliction through the ministerie of Satan vvas ioyned to excommunication. Where vve see also the diuels readines to inuade them that are cast out by excommunication, from the felovvship of the faithful, and the supereminent povver of Bishops in that case. Vvhereof S. Hierom ( ep. 1. ad Heliod. c. 7. ) hath these memorable vvordes: God forbid ( saith he ) I should speake sinistreously of them, vvho succeeding the Apostles in degree, make Christes body vvith their holy mouth, by vvhom vve are made Christians: vvho hauing the keies of heauen, do after a sort iudge before the day of iudgement: vvho in sobrietie and Chastitie haue the keeping of the spouse of Christ. And a litle after, They may deliuer me vp to Satan, to the destruction of my flesh, that the spirit may be saued in the day of our Lord Iesus. And in the old Lavv vvhosoeuer vvas disobedient to the Priests, vvas either cast out of the campe and so stoned of the people, or laying dovvne his necke to the svvord, expiated his offense by his bloud: but novv the disobedient is cut of vvith the spiritual svvord, or being cast out of the Church, is torne by the furious mouth of Diuels. So saith he. Vvhich vvordes vvould God euery Christiā man vvould vveigh.

notes.text: Excommunication of Heretikes, and the effect thereof.
